title: French Onion Soup (Soupe à l’Oignon Gratinée)
description: French Onion Soup (Soupe à l’Oignon Gratinée) is a classic French Continental soup made with slowly caramelized onions simmered in rich beef stock, finished with toasted baguette slices topped with Gruyère cheese and broiled until golden and bubbling.

ingredients.title: For the Soup
items: Yellow onions – 1 kg (about 6 large), thinly sliced
Beef stock – 1.2 L (rich, homemade preferred; chicken stock if lighter flavor is desired)
Freshly ground black pepper – to taste

ingredients.title: For the Topping
items: French baguette – 8 slices, about 1.5 cm thick
Gruyère cheese – 200 g, grated (Emmental or Comté as substitutes)
Parmesan – 40 g, finely grated (optional, for extra sharpness)

instruction.title: Step 1 – Caramelize the Onions
steps: In a heavy-bottomed pot, melt the butter with olive oil over medium-low heat.
Add the sliced onions with a pinch of salt. Cook slowly, stirring often, until deep golden brown and caramelized (35–40 minutes).
Chef’s tip: Keep the heat low and steady—patience creates sweetness and depth.

instruction.title: Step 2 – Build the Soup
steps: Add the garlic, thyme, and bay leaf; cook for 1–2 minutes until fragrant.
Deglaze with white wine, scraping up caramelized bits from the bottom. Reduce by half.
Pour in hot beef stock, stir, and bring to a simmer. Cover loosely and cook 25–30 minutes.
Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper. Remove thyme sprigs and bay leaf.

instruction.title: Step 3 – Prepare the Bread & Cheese
steps: Lightly toast baguette slices until crisp.
Top each slice generously with Gruyère (and a touch of Parmesan).

instruction.title: Step 4 – Assemble & Finish
steps: Ladle hot soup into oven-proof bowls.
Place cheesy baguette slices on top.
Place bowls under a hot broiler until the cheese melts, bubbles, and turns golden brown.

servingSuggestions.title: Serving Suggestions
items: Serve hot as a starter or soup course.
Pair with a crisp green salad or crusty French bread.
Enjoy with a glass of dry white wine.

chefTips: Keep the heat low and steady—patience creates sweetness and depth.
Serve in traditional French onion soup bowls with handles.
Garnish with a small thyme sprig or a drizzle of extra virgin olive oil.
Ensure cheese slightly overflows the bowl’s rim for that authentic restaurant look.
